title: Fixed coupon or percentage
hook: €5 off and 20% off cross over at a particular basket size.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Find the crossover of fixed and percentage discounts.

misconception: A percentage discount is always larger than a fixed coupon.
objective: Find the crossover of fixed and percentage discounts.

claims.text: A fictional basket can receive either 20% off or €5 off, with no exclusions. Scaled model; fictional offers; one coupon only.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Basket=20€, A=€16 and B=€15. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x",0.8]; B=["-","x",5]; x denotes Basket. At x=20, A=16, B=15; recall at x=23: B=18. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: The percentage scales with the basket; the fixed deduction does not. Their deductions match at €25 because 20% of €25 is €5. The lower result depends on the basket size.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x",0.8]; B=["-","x",5]; x denotes Basket. At x=20, A=16, B=15; recall at x=23: B=18. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: A fictional basket can receive either 20% off or €5 off, with no exclusions. Change only Basket to 23€. What is B (€5-off) now? Correct: €18. Use B's stated rule with Basket=23€: it gives €18. The percentage scales with the basket; the fixed deduction does not. Their deductions match at €25 because 20% of €25 is €5. The lower result depends on the basket size.

At x=20, A=16, B=15; recall at x=23: B=18. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

recall.question: A fictional basket can receive either 20% off or €5 off, with no exclusions. Change only Basket to 23€. What is B (€5-off) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Basket=23€: it gives €18. The percentage scales with the basket; the fixed deduction does not. Their deductions match at €25 because 20% of €25 is €5. The lower result depends on the basket size.

safety.assumptions: A fictional basket can receive either 20% off or €5 off, with no exclusions.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
